title: Location data linkability
description: Regular GPS coordinate transmissions can be linked across time to create movement patterns, or linked with other data sources to build comprehensive profiles of the child's activities and locations.
assumptions: Backend stores and processes location data over time

title: Child identifiability from location data
description: GPS coordinates transmitted at regular intervals can identify the specific child, especially when combined with device identifiers or account information stored at the backend.
assumptions: Backend maintains association between GPS data and child identity

title: Non-repudiation of location transmission
description: The child's device automatically transmits GPS data, making it difficult for the child to deny or control when location data is sent to the backend.
assumptions: Automatic transmission without explicit per-transmission consent

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: Live GPS coordinates are sensitive personal data that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through backend vulnerabilities, insider threats, or data breaches.
assumptions: Backend stores or processes location data

title: Location data aggregation
description: Regular GPS transmissions enable aggregation of location data over time, creating detailed movement profiles that reveal patterns about the child's daily routine, habits, and frequented locations.
assumptions: Backend retains historical location data

title: Child unawareness of location tracking
description: The child may not be fully aware that their location is being continuously tracked and transmitted to the backend, especially if they are young or if the tracking is not clearly communicated.
assumptions: Child is the data subject and may lack full understanding of data processing

title: Non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Processing children's location data may violate regulations such as COPPA (US) or GDPR-K (EU) if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, and parental controls are not implemented.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with children's privacy protections
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation details

title: Location pings can be linked to identify individual movement patterns
description: Location history data written to the store can be linked across time to reconstruct an individual's movement patterns, habits, and routines, enabling profiling and tracking.
assumptions: Location data includes timestamps and coordinates that can be correlated

title: Location data can directly identify individuals
description: Location history is highly identifying personal data that can reveal home addresses, workplaces, and sensitive locations, potentially identifying specific individuals.
assumptions: Location data is stored with user identifiers or can be linked to user accounts

title: Unauthorized access to location history store
description: If the Location History Store is compromised or accessed without authorization, sensitive location data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data store has access controls that could be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Excessive collection of location data
description: The system may be collecting more location data than necessary (e.g., continuous tracking vs. on-demand), violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Location pings are written for each event without clear necessity justification
uncertainty_note: Depends on business requirements and data retention policies

title: Users unaware of location data storage
description: Users may not be fully aware that their location pings are being stored in a persistent data store, or the extent of this storage.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate location data storage practices

title: Excessive location data forwarded to Geofencing Engine
description: The Mobile App Backend may forward more location data than necessary to the Geofencing Engine. Location pings could include unnecessary precision, frequency, or metadata beyond what's required for zone entry/exit detection, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Backend forwards raw location pings without filtering or aggregation

title: Location data enables user identification and tracking
description: The Geofencing Engine receives location pings that can identify individual users and track their movements over time. Even if anonymized at the source, location data combined with timing patterns can re-identify users.
assumptions: Location pings contain or can be linked to user identifiers

title: Users unaware of location data forwarding to Geofencing Engine
description: Users may not be fully informed that their location data is being forwarded from the Backend to a separate Geofencing Engine process. This lack of transparency about internal data flows reduces user awareness of how their location data is processed.
assumptions: Privacy policy does not detail internal process-to-process data flows

title: Unauthorized access to location data in Geofencing Engine
description: The Geofencing Engine process may be accessible to unauthorized personnel or systems, potentially exposing sensitive location data. Internal process boundaries may not have adequate access controls.
assumptions: Process P2 has access controls that could be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Unauthorized disclosure of zone definitions
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house locations) stored in the Family Account Store could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data store is compromised or access controls are bypassed. This reveals sensitive location information about family members' routines and personal spaces.
assumptions: Data store has access controls; zone definitions contain identifiable location data

title: Zone definitions enable identification of family members
description: Zone definitions may contain or be associated with information that identifies specific family members (e.g., 'John's school', 'Sarah's friend's house'), enabling identification of individuals through their location patterns.
assumptions: Zone names or configurations may reference specific individuals

title: Aggregation of zone data with location tracking
description: Zone definitions from the Family Account Store, when combined with real-time location data processed by the Geofencing Engine, could be aggregated to create detailed profiles of family members' movement patterns, routines, and social connections.
assumptions: Geofencing Engine processes location data alongside zone definitions

title: Family members unaware of zone data usage
description: Family members may not be fully aware that their location zone definitions are being read and used by the Geofencing Engine, or how this data contributes to alert generation and monitoring.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain zone data usage

title: Location data linkable to child identity
description: Geofencing notifications sent to the parent link the child's location movements (zone entry/exit events) to their identity, creating a persistent link between location data and personal identity.
assumptions: Notifications contain or can be correlated with child identity information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location notifications
description: Location-based arrival/departure notifications could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission from the Geofencing Engine to the parent.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be fully secured

title: Location data aggregation over time
description: Multiple geofencing notifications over time can be aggregated to build a detailed profile of the child's movement patterns, habits, and routines beyond individual zone events.
assumptions: Notifications are stored or logged over time

title: Child unaware of location monitoring
description: The child may not be aware that their location is being continuously monitored and that notifications are being sent to the parent when they enter or exit defined zones.
assumptions: Child may not have been informed about the geofencing system

title: Non-compliance with minor privacy regulations
description: Location tracking and notification of minors may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR) regarding consent, data minimization, and parental rights.
assumptions: System may not have proper consent mechanisms for location tracking of minors
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation details

title: Linkability of registration data to child tracking data
description: Parent registration data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) can be linked to subsequent location tracking and activity data, creating a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and habits.
assumptions: System stores and correlates registration data with ongoing location/activity data

title: Direct identification of parent and child
description: Registration data includes directly identifying information (parent name, child name, DOB, school) that can uniquely identify both individuals.
assumptions: Data is stored in a form that preserves direct identifiers

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive child information
description: Child's personal information (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or insecure transmission.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage may have security vulnerabilities

title: Aggregation of registration data with other child data
description: Registration data can be aggregated with location tracking, activity logs, and other data sources to create detailed behavioral profiles of the child beyond what was explicitly consented to.
assumptions: System collects and stores multiple data types about the child

title: Parent unawareness of data collection scope
description: Parent may not fully understand the extent of data collection, particularly regarding geofence zones and how location data will be used, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Privacy policy or consent mechanism may not clearly explain all data uses

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Collection of child data (name, DOB, school, location) may not comply with regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws requiring parental consent and data minimization.
assumptions: System may not have adequate compliance measures for child data
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Linkability of child profiles to accounts and locations
description: Child profile data stored in DS2 can be linked to specific family accounts and geofence zones, enabling correlation of children's identities with their locations and family relationships.
assumptions: Data store contains structured relationships between accounts, child profiles, and geofence zones

title: Identifiability of children through stored profile data
description: Child profile data stored in DS2 may contain or enable identification of individual children, especially when combined with account and geofence information.
assumptions: Child profiles contain personally identifiable information or can be used to identify specific children

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored personal data
description: Account, child profile, and geofence zone data stored in DS2 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data store compromise, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Data store has potential vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Excessive data collection beyond minimality principle
description: The storage of account, child profile, and geofence zone data may exceed what is strictly necessary for the application's purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Some stored data fields may not be essential for core functionality
uncertainty_note: Assessment of data minimality requires detailed schema review

title: User unawareness of data storage practices
description: Users may not be fully aware of what account, child profile, and geofence data is being stored, how long it is retained, or what purposes it serves.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data storage practices

title: Limited user control over stored personal data
description: Users may have limited ability to access, correct, or delete their account, child profile, and geofence zone data stored in DS2.
assumptions: Data management interfaces may not provide comprehensive user controls

title: Location data linkability to child identity
description: The child's location data transmitted to the parent can be linked to their identity and other personal data, enabling tracking of movements and activities over time.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient precision to identify the child's whereabouts

title: Child identifiability through location patterns
description: Location history and current location data can reveal the child's identity through movement patterns, frequented locations, and behavioral signatures.
assumptions: Location data is precise enough to identify individual movement patterns

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child location data
description: Location data could be intercepted during transmission or accessed by unauthorized parties through the mobile app backend, exposing the child's whereabouts.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or backend may have security vulnerabilities

title: Aggregation of location history reveals sensitive patterns
description: Accumulated location history data can be aggregated to reveal sensitive information about the child's routines, habits, social connections, and frequented places.
assumptions: Location history is stored and can be queried over time

title: Child unaware of location tracking and sharing
description: The child may not be aware that their location is being tracked and shared with the parent, violating their right to know about data processing.
assumptions: Children may not understand or consent to location tracking

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Location tracking of minors may violate regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws requiring parental consent, data minimization, and age-appropriate safeguards.
assumptions: System may not implement proper consent mechanisms or data protection for minors

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location History
description: Location history data stored in DS1 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data store is compromised or access controls are insufficient. This is particularly sensitive as location history can reveal personal patterns, routines, and private locations.
assumptions: Data store has appropriate access controls in place

title: Identifiability Through Location History
description: Location history data is inherently identifying and could be used to identify specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources. Even anonymized location data can often be re-identified.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity for identification

title: Data Aggregation and Profiling
description: Location history retrieved from DS1 could be aggregated with other data to create detailed user profiles, revealing sensitive information about habits, associations, and personal life that exceeds the original purpose of collection.
assumptions: Backend has access to multiple data sources for aggregation

title: User Unawareness of Data Retrieval
description: Users (parents/children) may not be fully aware that their location history is being retrieved and used for map/history views, or may not understand the extent of data processing involved.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data retrieval activities

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The retrieval and processing of location history may not fully comply with applicable privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, COPPA) regarding purpose limitation, data minimization, and consent requirements for location data.
assumptions: Location data processing requires specific consent under applicable regulations

title: Linkability between parent, secondary guardian, and child
description: The invitation flow creates linkability between the parent (EE1), the secondary guardian being invited, and the child whose location is being shared. This enables correlation of identities and activities across multiple parties.
assumptions: The backend processes and stores invitation relationships

title: Direct identification of parent and secondary guardian
description: The parent's identity and the secondary guardian's identity are transmitted to the backend, making both parties directly identifiable in the system.
assumptions: Identity information is included in the invitation request

title: Disclosure of child location access permissions
description: The backend receives and processes information about who has access to the child's location data, which is sensitive information about the child's privacy settings and trusted contacts.
assumptions: Location access permissions are stored and processed by the backend

title: Unawareness of data processing by secondary guardian
description: The secondary guardian being invited may not be fully aware of what data will be processed about them or the child once they accept the invitation.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not be clear about data processing implications

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Sharing child location data with additional guardians may require specific consent mechanisms under regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K, which may not be properly implemented.
assumptions: The system handles child data subject to privacy regulations

title: Location data linkability to child identity
description: The child's live location data shared with the secondary guardian can be linked to the child's identity, creating a persistent link between location history and personal identity that could be used to track movements over time.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient precision to identify the child's whereabouts

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child location
description: The child's live location could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the secondary guardian shares it further, or if there's a security breach in the backend system during transmission.
assumptions: Secondary guardian may not have adequate security controls; transmission could be intercepted

title: Location data aggregation creating movement profile
description: Multiple live location data points shared over time can be aggregated to create a detailed movement profile of the child, revealing patterns about their daily routine, habits, and frequented locations.
assumptions: Location data is shared continuously or frequently over time

title: Child unaware of location sharing with secondary guardian
description: The child may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, or may not understand the scope and implications of this data sharing.
assumptions: Child may not have been informed or may not comprehend the privacy implications

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Sharing child's live location with secondary guardian may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding consent, data minimization, or purpose limitation for children's data.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements exist for children's location data sharing
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory compliance depends on jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Linkability of analytics data to user profiles
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with advertising partners can be linked to other data sources to build comprehensive user profiles, enabling cross-service tracking and behavioral profiling.
assumptions: Advertising partners maintain user profiles and can correlate analytics data with other identifiers

title: Re-identification from aggregated analytics
description: Even aggregated analytics data can potentially be de-anonymized through re-identification attacks, especially when combined with other data sources held by the advertising partner.
assumptions: Sufficient auxiliary data exists for re-identification attacks on aggregated datasets

title: Data aggregation across multiple sources
description: Analytics data from this flow contributes to advertising partners' ability to aggregate data from multiple apps and services, creating detailed user profiles beyond what users expect.
assumptions: Advertising partners aggregate data from multiple third-party sources

title: User unawareness of data sharing extent
description: Users may not fully understand that 'aggregated analytics' are shared with advertising partners, or the extent to which this data can be used for profiling and targeted advertising.
assumptions: Privacy policies do not clearly communicate the implications of analytics data sharing

title: Potential regulatory compliance issues
description: Sharing usage analytics with advertising partners may require specific legal basis under GDPR/CCPA, including explicit consent for secondary purposes beyond app functionality.
assumptions: Data sharing may not have proper legal basis or user consent for advertising purposes
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific consent mechanisms and privacy policy language

title: Location data linkability to child identity
description: The child's location data sent in check-in/SOS messages can be linked to their identity and combined with other data flows to create a comprehensive movement profile.
assumptions: Child's identity is known to the system and location data is stored/processed

title: Child identifiability from location data
description: The check-in/SOS message with current location directly identifies the specific child, making them identifiable from this data flow.
assumptions: Location data is unique enough to identify the child

title: Attributable check-in/SOS messages

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child location

title: Location data aggregation reveals movement patterns
